question.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,1⟩, \\ N(t) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,1⟩\times ⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 3\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 1 \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 1 \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 1 \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 3\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨(0+\operatorname{sin}⁡t),-(0+\operatorname{cos}⁡t),(3{sin}^{2}⁡t+3{cos}^{2}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
